observed_findings.detail: SkiaSharp.Views.WPF 4.153.1 restored OpenTK/OpenTK.GLWpfControl through .NET Framework compatibility under net10.0-windows and emitted NU1701; warning suppression is not accepted.

observed_evidence.detail: SkiaSharp 4.153.1 offscreen adapter executed through MotionKit runtime; deterministic frame hash, Full/Reduced distinction, lifecycle, unsupported capability and 100-frame batch observation passed.
net10.0-windows WPF project using core SkiaSharp 4.153.1 and SKBitmap-to-BitmapSource bridge built successfully without suppressing NU1701.
600 core-Skia BitmapSource updates in visible WPF window, session 5, normal process exit 0. Static bridge fixture, not product animation.

Reference Windows probe passed S1, S3, S4 and S5 in Full and Reduced Motion with native WPF keyboard/accessibility surface, deterministic RETURN/fallback, renderer disposal/re-entry and dense-screen measurements. S2 remains unassigned because no accepted role currently claims STATEFUL_VECTOR.

WASDK ContentIsland + DesktopChildSiteBridge attached to WPF HWND. Full opacity pixel changes, Reduced static settle, normal process exit 0. Original API probe also exits 0.

observed_findings.detail: The probe owned a Microsoft.UI DispatcherQueueController, ran an explicit DispatcherQueue event loop, created/used Composition API objects, then still exceeded the 15 second process shutdown budget on the headless GitHub Windows runner. Runtime lifecycle is deferred to an interactive/reference Windows environment; no custom workaround will be invented in shared MotionKit.
observed_findings.superseded_for: Interactive/reference Windows deferral resolved by COMPOSITION_YASSIN_WPF_WINDOW_PASS; original headless timeout remains historical.

source_evidence.detail: Exact rive-runtime source commit pinned; repository LICENSE is MIT.
Repository documents Windows native C++ build/toolchain and D3D11/D3D12 renderer backends; this does not prove .NET/WPF integration.

observed_findings.detail: Initial official build generation reached Rive dependency checkout and failed on a HarfBuzz filename exceeding default Windows Git path limits. Enabling core.longpaths resolved the environment limitation without MotionKit code changes.

observed_evidence.detail: Pinned rive-runtime commit used the repository's official build_rive.ps1/build_rive.sh path and successfully generated tests/out/release/rive.sln on the Windows GitHub runner.
Search of the pinned rive-runtime source found no C# source binding/runtime project; .NET/WPF use would require a deliberately bounded native interop layer or another officially supported route.

source_evidence.detail: Repository LICENSE.md is MIT; current source head pinned separately from release tag.
Repository contains LottieGen .NET global tool for generating C#/C++ and other outputs from Lottie/Bodymovin JSON; README states .NET 7 SDK or later.
NuGet stable LottieGen 8.2.250604 targets .NET 9, is compatible with .NET 10, has no package dependencies, and is documented as the efficient Windows code-generation path.

observed_findings.detail: LottieGen 8.2.250604 help text advertises -StrictMode, but the command-line parser accepts Keyword.Strict; -StrictMode failed as Unexpected while -Strict is the source-backed strict parsing switch. The lab keeps strict parsing by using -Strict rather than weakening the probe.

Pinned LottieGen 8.2.250604 accepted -Strict but failed to find a repository-relative fixture on Ubuntu. Pinned Glob.cs appends a literal backslash to its directory path, so the deterministic codegen probe is moved to Windows rather than weakening Strict/TestMode.

observed_evidence.detail: Verified successful strict deterministic LottieGen Windows step; tooling only.

performance_disposition.reason: Reference-host WPF presentation-loop, CPU, allocation, memory and input observations are recorded; no post-hoc performance threshold is invented.

reference_windows_qualification.input_evidence_limit: Keyboard activation is actual WPF input; hover exercises the shared WPF hover-state handler. Hardware pointer injection is not claimed because the active reference-host game reclaims the OS cursor.
